Jordan L: Quick sync - Ivy asked for a private POC onboarding plan focused on BYOK + cert lifecycle. They want dev engineer access in ~48h. Can we get a runnable checklist and the minimal artifacts we need from them?

Amy S: Short answer: yes. Two paths: (1) BYOK via customer KMS (recommended for enterprise), or (2) temp Redwood-managed keys to speed POC. Will lay out both.

Marco P: For BYOK (AWS) the minimal items we need from Ivy: KMS key ARN with policy granting our service principal, VPC ID + subnet list for agent, a CA-signed agent cert (PEM), and (optional) a wrapped key blob if they insist on HSM-wrapped private key transfer.

Tess R: Security request: include expected rotation cadence, who holds escrow, and HSM attestation doc if they provide HSM. POC acceptance can use 30-day rotation but prod must meet our 7-day target.

Jordan L: Can you spell out commands they should run? Keep it copy-paste.

Marco P: Sure. KMS create-key example (they must substitute account/region):
```
aws kms create-key --description "Ivy POC key for Redwood" --policy file://redwood-policy.json
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/ivy-redwood-poc --target-key-id <key-id>
```
Then export the key ARN from the create-key result.

Marco P: CSR example we ask them to generate locally and sign with their CA:
```
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:3072 -out agent.key
openssl req -new -key agent.key -out agent.csr -subj "/CN=redwood-agent.ivy.poc/O=Ivy"
# Then have internal CA sign agent.csr -> agent.crt
```

Amy S: If they want fastest path, Redwood-managed key option: they sign an addendum (custodian NDA), we generate a single-use KMS key for the POC and rotate it at end-of-POC. No HSM attestation needed. Good for <24h setup.

Tess R: Also note networking: agent needs outbound to api.redwood-inference.internal:443 and access to S3 or presigned model URLs. If they run egress proxy-only, provide proxy details or we run an outbound relay image in their VPC.

Marco P: Minimal JSON we ask them to paste into the Console (literal):
```
{
  "customer": "Ivy",
  "env": "poC",
  "vpc_id": "vpc-0a1b2c3d",
  "subnets": ["subnet-aaa","subnet-bbb"],
  "kms_key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01",
  "agent_cert_crt": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----...",
  "agent_cert_key_enc": "base64-wrapped-key-or-empty-if-kept-local",
  "preferred_key_mode": "BYOK"
}
```

Jordan L: What about model pulls? They have strict egress and no S3. Can we support a pull via SSH bastion or peered ENI?

Marco P: Yes. Options: peered ENI, VPC peering, or an SSH bastion that the agent uses to pull model blobs. If no external S3, we can provide model via presigned URL delivered over the control plane connection. That requires agent to allow inbound from our control-plane IPs for a short TTL or use an outbound tunnel.

Tess R: For HSM scenarios: they can generate key material in their HSM and provide a wrapped key blob using PKCS#11 wrap. We'll need their public wrapping cert and a spec of the wrap algorithm. Also ask for attestation report (manufacturer/firmware).

Amy S: Pricing note from me: Private POC typically carries a short-term platform fee + optional support add-on. Dedicated trial might be cheaper infra-wise but doesn't meet BYOK requirements. I'll send a clean ballpark to Jordan in DM.

Jordan L: Legal + SLA: do we need an NDA addendum for key custody on Redwood-managed keys?

Tess R: Yes. For Redwood-managed keys during POC we require a limited-scope key custody addendum and 90d audit log retention. Legal will draft the short addendum.

oncall_bot: Onboarding checklist created: https://internal.redwood/onboard/1979129999. Steps: 1) Receive JSON + certs, 2) Validate KMS access, 3) Agent bootstrap, 4) Validation script.

Marco P: I'll drop a small validation script (encrypt/decrypt + cert handshake) into the internal gist and paste link here in ~40m.

Amy S: I'll send the customer-facing checklist and opt-in form for Redwood-managed key within 20m.

Jordan L: Perfect. I'll schedule the 48h window once Marco + Amy confirm artifacts. Thanks everyone.
